senses.gloss: נִמֵּר (denom. of preced.) to give a checkered or striped appearance, esp. נ׳ שדה to take out or cut the ripe plants of a field, leaving the unripe stand for later crops.
units: Men. 71ᵇ במְנַמֵּר לקליות when he cuts portions of the grain field with the intention of using the ears for roasting; במנמר לאוצר when he cuts for storage.—Part. pass. מְנוּמָּר striped, speckled.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 119b:8">B. Kam. 119ᵇ</cite> <he>לוקחין מהן בגד מנ׳</he> you may buy from them (weavers) (even) a checkered web (for which they may have used remnants of other people’s wool).

<cite ref="Gittin 54b:18">Gitt. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>משום דמיחזי כמנ׳</he> because (if he were to pass his pen over all the Divine Names in the scroll) the writing would look speckled; <cite ref="Menachot 29b:16">Men. 29ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>משום דמיחזי כמ׳</he> it would look speckled (if he were to insert omitted vowel letters).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3:10:2">Y. Succ. III, 53ᵈ</cite> bot.; Y. Maasr. I, 49ᵃ <cite ref="E00431"><he>המ׳</he></cite> a speckled Ethrog.
